findings.defect: The Korean adds that a sharp blade cuts off a whole handful of his hair. The assembled copy omits this physical detail, which the accepted baseline preserved.
findings.rationale: The source explicitly describes the chill and the loss of a handful of hair before describing the auras grazing his body.
findings.replacement:
*Slice! Spurt!*
A chill. I felt a sharp blade cut off a whole handful of my hair.

findings.current: At the same time, the world that had momentarily stopped began moving again.
findings.defect: The source explicitly says the silence shattered. That beat is absent from the assembled copy, though present in the accepted baseline.
findings.rationale: “산산이 부서지는 정적” establishes the silence breaking as a distinct beat before the world resumes moving.
findings.replacement: The silence shattered. At the same time, the world that had momentarily stopped began moving again.

findings.current: “God told me, you crazy old bastard.”
findings.defect: “Bastard” adds profanity not present in the Korean insult.
findings.rationale: “이 정신 나간 늙은이야” means a crazy or out-of-his-mind old man; it does not include a profanity equivalent to “bastard.”
findings.replacement: “God told me, you crazy old man.”

summary: The assembled copy has a few localized fidelity defects: it drops a physical detail and a silence-breaking beat, and it intensifies one insult.
